newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FOCUS-Australia links Toyota move to tariff stance.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Australia links Toyota move to tariff stance.

text.p: Japanese car-maker Toyota Motor Corp on Monday announced an expansion of Australian production in a move hailed by Canberra as vindication of its refusal to slash tariffs on foreign-made cars.
Toyota president Hiroshi Okuda, flanked by Prime Minister John Howard, told a news conference Toyota would begin making a new family car for the Australian market from year 2000.

The new project is part of a plan to spend up to A$1 billion upgrading Toyota's Melbourne plant over the next eight years, almost doubling its annual production to 140,000 cars by 2005, the company said.
The announcement comes two months after Howard rejected the recommendations of an official advisory body for an accelerated drop in tariffs to five percent by 2004 from 22.5 percent now.
Citing the need to protect an industry which employs over 45,000 people, Canberra instead stuck by the existing timetable for tariff cuts which would see them fall to 15 percent by 2000.
